202B.6 / CHAPTER 6 OF 11

Expansion & pullback

Is the decline testing the base or breaking it?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Price structure02Base & repricing03Supply zones04Demand & absorption05Holder rotation06Expansion & pullback07Continuation vs distribution08Swing lifecycle09Retracement references: 0.5 & 0.61810Comprehensive swing check11How to trade the swing

01Definition

Expansion moves out of a range. A pullback tests what buying remains after that move.

02Why it matters

The percentage decline alone cannot distinguish a retest from structural failure.

03What to check

  • The prior breakout area and base
  • Sell activity and subsequent recovery
  • Liquidity changes and external holder evidence

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

Selling cools and repeated buying stabilizes price near the prior area.

Dangerous

The base fails, rebounds weaken, and liquidity deteriorates.

05Beginner mistake

Calling every 30–50% drop either healthy or dead.

06Takeaway

Judge what the pullback does to the structure.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    Price expands from a range, then declines 35%.

  2. 02

    The prior breakout area holds through repeated tests.

  3. 03

    The decline may be a retest; a sustained loss of that area weakens the view.

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

A move from 1.00 to 1.40 retraces to 1.20. That pullback differs from falling below the original 1.00 area with declining depth. The percentage decline alone does not reveal whether selling was absorbed.

How to investigate it

Mark the original base and expansion, then examine sell size, recovery, and current liquidity during the pullback. Compare actual activity with the earlier breakout window. Set the evidence that would invalidate continuation before describing every cheaper print as an opportunity.

Check your reasoning — answered

Price retraces mildly but the pool loses most of its liquidity. Is the shallow chart pullback enough to preserve the case? No. Executable conditions worsened independently of the chart.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Inspect

Use available historical candles for ranges and returned swaps for observed flow. Candle volume does not provide a buy/sell split.

Go deeper

Base → expansion → pullback → continuation is one possible path. Specify what would count as a failed retest before interpreting every rebound as confirmation.
